message:
`hex_to_u32` reads 4 bytes: `c[0]`, `c[1]`, `c[2]`, `c[3]`. The check in `handle_unicode_code_point` is `if (it + 4 >= end)`, which means it requires `it + 4 < end`, i.e., `it + 4 <= end - 1`, so `it + 3 <= end - 2`. That means `c[3]` is at most `end - 2`, which is safe. Wait, let me re-check.

`it + 4 >= end` means we return false (error). So we proceed only when `it + 4 < end`, i.e., `it + 4 <= end - 1`, so `it + 3 <= end - 2`. Reading `c[3] = it[3]` is safe since `it[3] <= end - 2 < end`.

Hmm, that seems fine. But wait - the issue says "READ 5". Let me look at the surrogate pair case. After reading the high surrogate (4 bytes), it checks `if (it + 6 >= end)`. So it requires `it + 6 < end`, i.e., `it + 5 <= end - 2`. Then it does `std::memcpy(&u, it, 2)` reading 2 bytes at `it` and `it+1`, which is safe. Then `hex_to_u32(it)` reads 4 bytes at `it` through `it+3`. Since `it + 5 <= end - 2`, we have `it + 3 <= end - 4`, which is safe.

Wait, let me reconsider. The check `it + 6 >= end` means we need `it + 6 < end`, so `it + 5 <= end - 1`, meaning `it + 5 < end`. So `it + 3 < end - 2`, safe.

Hmm, let me look at the actual issue more carefully. The issue is "Heap-buffer-overflow READ 5". Let me look at the `skip_string_view` function or the `skip_string` function which might have similar issues:

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<parameter=command>cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/glaze && grep -n "skip_string_view\|skip_string" include/glaze/json/read.hpp | head -20</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
